name: Aave sDAI Ethereum phishing
technique: Malicious off-chain permit signature; Phishing/social engineering; Potential use of CREATE2 temporary contract address for plausibility
classificationNote: Classified by TypeSafe jev-1.13.0 (confidence 1.00). Replaced keyword guess "signature-crypto".
rootCause: On October 10, 2024, an Aave sDAI holder on Ethereum lost approximately 2,229,311 sDAI (worth about $2.47 million) after being deceived by a phishing campaign. The attacker obtained a malicious permit signature from the victim, enabling the unauthorized transfer of sDAI. The exploit relied on social engineering, possibly using precomputed addresses via CREATE2, but the precise phishing delivery method remains unverified. The incident resulted from the victim signing a malicious permit signature after falling for a phishing scam. The permit enabled the attacker to transfer all sDAI tokens from the victim’s account. No protocol or contract vulnerability…
